entries.senior_programs: Medicaid buy-in for working people with disabilities: monthly premium billed by the state while enrolled.
entries.notes: Alaska DPA manual 534: premiums set on a sliding scale (none below 100% FPG, max 10% of family net income) and billed/collected by the Division of Health Care Services Third Party Liability Unit (contact email doh.hcs.rec.info@alaska.gov); first premium due the second month after notice; coverage ends at 60 days delinquent and back premiums must be paid before reopening. Applicants 65+ with substantial earnings can qualify (relevant to working seniors). The Division of Health Care Services Third Party Liability Unit sets the premium, mails the notice of premium due and collects payment (email doh.hcs.rec.info@alaska.gov). No one under 100% of the poverty guideline pays, and no one pays more than 10% of annual net family income. No automatic payment option is offered; pay each premium notice by the method printed on it.

entries.notes: Members should use the number on their plan ID card. Trinity Health PACE (Trinity Health Corporation, about 3,100 participants in 12 programs). Eligibility Requirements page: services are typically free to seniors who qualify for Medicare and Medicaid or Medicaid only; participants who do not qualify for Medicaid are charged a monthly fee and may pay privately; enrollment is not restricted by Medicare/Medicaid status. Each program has its own page and contact-us page on trinityhealthpace.org (state/program paths, e.g. /alabama/mercy-life-of-alabama/contact-us). No online payment, autopay or mailing address is published - call the PACE center. They pointed to the Eligibility Requirements page, which explains who pays (Medicaid-eligible participants usually pay nothing; others pay a monthly fee or pay privately) but not how to view or pay a bill. The Trinity Health PACE FAQ  says payment depends on Medicare/Medicaid eligibility and over-income/asset participants pay monthly fees. Program contact page  gives the phone numbers now recorded. Call the center about private-pay fees. Member-cost page, used because no plan premium is billed to most participants. The program's eligibility page  says services are 'typically free to seniors who qualify for Medicare and Medicaid or Medicaid only'. Participants who do not qualify for Medicaid are charged a monthly fee and may pay privately. There is no copay or deductible, and the monthly private-pay amount is set by the program. No online payment, autopay, statement or paperless page is published; private-pay participants arrange billing with the program office (see phone).

entries.notes: Members should use the number on their plan ID card. Trinity Health PACE (Trinity Health Corporation, about 3,100 participants in 12 programs). Eligibility Requirements page: services are typically free to seniors who qualify for Medicare and Medicaid or Medicaid only; participants who do not qualify for Medicaid are charged a monthly fee and may pay privately; enrollment is not restricted by Medicare/Medicaid status. Each program has its own page and contact-us page on trinityhealthpace.org (state/program paths, e.g. /alabama/mercy-life-of-alabama/contact-us). No online payment, autopay or mailing address is published - call the PACE center. They pointed to the Eligibility Requirements page, which explains who pays (Medicaid-eligible participants usually pay nothing; others pay a monthly fee or pay privately) but not how to view or pay a bill. The Trinity Health PACE FAQ  says payment depends on Medicare/Medicaid eligibility and over-income/asset participants pay monthly fees. Program contact page  gives the phone numbers now recorded. Call the center about private-pay fees. Member-cost page, used because no plan premium is billed to most participants. The program's eligibility page  says services are 'typically free to seniors who qualify for Medicare and Medicaid or Medicaid only'. Participants who do not qualify for Medicaid are charged a monthly fee and may pay privately. There is no copay or deductible, and the monthly private-pay amount is set by the program. No online payment, autopay, statement or paperless page is published; private-pay participants arrange billing with the program office (see phone).

entries.notes: Pay My Premium page is DHS's common premium-payment page for MinnesotaCare and MA-EPD. Two other official DHS sites were readable. (1) DHS Web Payments (payments.dhs.state.mn.us) lists MA-EPD under "State of MN-Product 3" (shared with AC, MSHO and SNBC). It takes the customer number and the first 4 letters of the last name from the invoice and accepts one-time or recurring payments through U.S. Bank E-Payment. To stop an existing recurring payment, use the link on the same page; to change the amount, stop the recurring payment and set up a new one. (2) The Eligibility Policy Manual 2.3.5.1.2 (hcopub.dhs.state.mn.us) says the county or tribal agency bills and collects the initial premium, which must be paid within 30 days. After that DHS mails a monthly invoice with the premium and due date; past-due amounts and credits are not shown on it. Premiums are due on the 4th but accepted through the last working day of the month. After a non-payment closure, two months of premium must be paid to reinstate. Ongoing payments can be made by mail, in person or online. On the DHS payment page you enter the first 4 letters of the last name on the invoice and the amount, or log in to an existing account. The same page has a link to stop an existing recurring payment; to change a recurring amount, stop it and set up a new one. American Indian and Alaska Native enrollees who verify status are exempt from MA-EPD premiums.

entries.senior_programs: Medicaid spend-down / excess income: seniors whose income is over the Medicaid limit can qualify each month by incurring medical bills or, in some states, paying the excess amount to the state ('pay-in').
entries.notes: Combined Medicaid Manual CMA 701-1 "Cash Option" (effective 1/1/2022). Medically needy clients may meet their monthly spend down by paying the exact spend-down amount in cash to the Department. Once the payment is processed, Medicaid is issued for the full month. The amount can be reduced by allowable expenses: paid or unpaid medical bills from the 3 prior months, health insurance and Medicare premiums, and non-covered medical expenses. The cash option is not available to people receiving VA Aid & Attendance. It can be used for retroactive months. The manual gives no payment address; the spend-down notice from the local Office of Public Assistance gives remittance instructions. No automatic payment option; pay the exact monthly spend-down amount to DPHHS for each month you want coverage, or meet it with medical bills.

Payment history: Medicare account > My premiums > Payment history. Most people have Part B deducted from Social Security, RRB or OPM annuity and never receive a bill. Official page says credit card by mail via coupon; there is no pay-by-phone option listed. Medicare Easy Pay page  answers 'How do I change bank accounts or stop Medicare Easy Pay?' entries.name: Social Security Administration - Medicare premium deductions & IRMAA (Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount)
entries.service_area_detail: Nationwide. SSA deducts Part B premium, Part B IRMAA and Part D IRMAA from Social Security benefits; people not receiving benefits get IRMAA billed by CMS on the Medicare Premium Bill (CMS-500). Part D IRMAA is paid to Medicare, not to the drug plan. Also where MA/PDP plan premiums are withheld (premium withhold option).
entries.payment_processor: Social Security benefit withholding; otherwise CMS bill
entries.senior_programs: Request lower IRMAA after a life-changing event (marriage, divorce, death of spouse, work stoppage/loss of income, employer settlement) with Form SSA-44: sign in and submit online, or fax/mail to a local office. Call 1-800-772-1213 for amended tax returns. Apply for Part D Extra Help online at ssa.gov/medicare/part-d-extra-help.
entries.notes: IRMAA amounts for 2026 are also published by RRB (rrb.gov news release). For the app: an IRMAA notice is not a separate bill if premiums are withheld from benefits; if not, IRMAA appears on the CMS Medicare Premium Bill and is paid via Medicare. The Lower IRMAA page links the SSA-44 PDF and the online SSA-44 upload flow. The Extra Help page has an online application. The Manage Medicare benefits page says people whose premiums are not withheld from Social Security are billed by CMS, and lists the ways to pay Medicare (online account, Easy Pay, bank bill pay, mail to the Medicare Premium Collection Center). SSA itself has no pay-by-phone or autopay service for premiums. SSA itself has no autopay enrollment page: Social Security withholding of Part B, IRMAA and (on request through the plan) Medicare Advantage/Part D premiums happens automatically from monthly benefits. To start or stop withholding of a private plan premium, the member contacts the plan (see each carrier's 'ssa_rrb_premium_deduction' link); withholding changes typically take 1-3 months. Medicare Supplement premiums cannot be withheld by SSA.

entries.notes: Premium payments page  covers Medicare Supplement: one-time debit/credit card payment; automatic monthly ACH from checking/savings on a date you choose (ACH payment option form, email billing@wpsic.com or fax 608-223-3639) or recurring card; remove/update payment method at least 7 business days before due date; pay by phone; mail check to address on Billing Statement; invoices generated on the 5th for premium due the 1st of next month. Grace period for Medicare supplement policies: 31 days after due date, coverage stays in force during grace (IFP plans differ). Medicare Supplement member page  FAQ: guaranteed renewable while premium is paid. WPS premium-payments page confirms Medicare Supplement invoices are generated around the 5th for the payment due on the 1st of the next month and a 31-day grace period during which coverage stays in force.

entries.senior_programs: Medicaid buy-in for working people with disabilities: monthly premium billed by the state while enrolled.
entries.notes: WDH Eligibility Online Manual M1003: premium = 7.5% of gross monthly income (less $50 of unearned); first two months free, third month prepaid by the 10th; fiscal agent mails payment coupons; mail premiums to the lockbox above. Program ends at age 65 (case closes when client turns 65), so it rarely applies to seniors. The fiscal agent mails payment coupons; mail premiums with the coupon to State of Wyoming - EID Premiums, P.O. Box 200120, Dallas, TX 75320-0120. No automatic payment option is offered; pay each premium notice by the method printed on it.
